rics.meaning: Federal debt total amount outstanding — Treasury's gross debt position including all marketable securities (bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, FRNs) and nonmarketable issuances (savings bonds, intragovernmental).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks the running tally of Treasury issuance. The marketable-debt subset (~$27T) is what funds the actual federal deficit; nonmarketable debt is mostly Trust Fund holdings. Issuance pattern (bills vs notes/bonds) signals Treasury's term-structure strategy.

rics.meaning: Public debt outstanding — total Treasury debt held by both the public and intragovernmental accounts (Trust Funds). The 'gross debt' measure mentioned in headlines around the debt ceiling.
rics.how_to_use: ~$36T in 2025. The 'debt held by the public' subset (~$28T) is the more economically meaningful measure since intragovernmental debt is a Treasury IOU to itself. Watch debt-ceiling negotiations — extraordinary measures kick in when ceiling is hit.

rics.description: GROSS PUBLIC DEBT AS % OF GDP
rics.meaning: Gross public debt as a percentage of GDP — the standard sustainability gauge using gross (not net of intragovernmental) debt. Higher than debt-held-by-public/GDP by ~25-30 percentage points.
rics.how_to_use: CBO projects debt/GDP rising to 120-130% by 2034 absent policy change. Threshold concerns vary: most economists view 100-120% as 'manageable for reserve currency issuer'; >150% historically associated with fiscal crisis. Watch debt-service/GDP ratio for nearer-term signal.

rics.meaning: Total Treasury securities outstanding (public debt). Sum of bills, notes, bonds, plus nonmarketable.
rics.how_to_use: Supply pipeline for Treasury auctions. Acceleration in growth implies more issuance, pressure on term premium.

rics.meaning: Treasury bills outstanding — short-term debt (≤1Y). The bulk of refinancing risk sits here.
rics.how_to_use: Heavy bill issuance keeps front-end yields elevated and TGA management active. Watch as % of total marketable debt — rising share signals fiscal stress.

rics.meaning: Treasury bonds outstanding — long-term coupon debt (>10Y). Mostly 20Y and 30Y bonds.
rics.how_to_use: Long-end supply impacts term premium. Bond issuance schedule announced in quarterly refunding. Demand monitored via primary dealer takedowns and indirect bidder share.

rics.description: Treasury securities outstanding, nonmarketable, government account series
rics.meaning: Nonmarketable Treasury securities held in government account series (Social Security, federal pensions, etc).
rics.how_to_use: Doesn't trade in markets; subtract from gross debt to get marketable supply. Mainly accounting interest.

rics.meaning: Treasury notes outstanding — coupon debt (2Y to 10Y maturity).
rics.how_to_use: Belly of the curve — the most common duration target for asset managers. Watch 10Y note auction stats for global demand signal.

rics.meaning: Total marketable Treasury securities — bills + notes + bonds + TIPS + FRNs. The free-float bond supply (excluding non-marketable issues like savings bonds).
rics.how_to_use: Compare against M2 to see Treasury vs broad money balance. Bills (≤1Y) currently ~20% of marketable supply — historically high; signals refinancing stress. Issuance schedule announced quarterly in Refunding Statement.
